sections.heading: Traffic stops and general licensing
sections.markdown:
## Traffic stops and general licensing

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
An officer may stop a vehicle on reasonable suspicion of a traffic or criminal violation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=5]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01
When an officer signals a stop, signal your own movement, pull safely beside or off the road, switch off the engine and audio, and remain inside unless directed otherwise. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=5]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A01
During a nighttime traffic stop, turn on the passenger-compartment light. Keep hands visible and follow the officer's instructions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=5]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A01
An officer may approach either side of the vehicle. Open the window on that side so the officer can communicate with you. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=5]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A01
At the first contact during a stop, tell the officer if a weapon is in the vehicle. Await instructions before reaching for documents. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=5]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A01
A driver may request identification when an officer in plain clothes has not displayed credentials. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=5]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A01
At a stop, the officer generally explains the reason and may ask about the trip. Be prepared to provide the driver's license, registration and insurance evidence. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=5]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A01
If requested documents are beyond easy reach, explain where they are and wait for the officer to acknowledge you before retrieving them. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=5]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A01
When told to leave the vehicle, keep your hands visible and stand where the officer directs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=5]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A01
A traffic stop can end with a warning, a traffic ticket that may carry a fine, or an arrest, and the officer usually explains the action being taken [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=5]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A01
Ask for clarification respectfully. A disputed citation can be contested in court; prolonging an argument at the roadside is discouraged. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=5]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A01
Signing a traffic citation does not admit guilt. Refusing the signature may result in arrest. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=5]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A01
For concerns about an officer's conduct, the handbook recommends requesting a supervisor as soon as practicable after the stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=5]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A02
A person who becomes a Georgia resident and wants to drive on Georgia roads must obtain the state's license or permit within 30 days. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=6]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A02
Georgia residency includes having a permanent home in the state with an intention to return when away. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=6]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A02
Accepting work or conducting a trade in Georgia, enrolling one's children in school there, or remaining in the state for at least 30 days can establish residency under the handbook's criteria. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=6]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A02
A federal government employee driving a vehicle owned by or leased to the United States government, or driving on official business, is exempt from needing a Georgia license unless the federal government or one of its agencies requires a state license [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=6]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A02
A nonresident aged at least 16 may drive with a valid home-state or home-country license in immediate possession, while remaining subject to applicable Georgia driving restrictions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=6]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A02
A nonresident serving on active duty in the United States armed forces may use a valid home-state license. The same exception covers a spouse or dependent child with a valid home-state license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=6]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A02
Someone serving on active duty in the United States armed forces who carries a valid license issued abroad by the United States armed forces may drive with it for up to forty-five days after returning to the United States [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=6]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A02
A person temporarily operating a tractor or other farm equipment on a highway for farm business is within the handbook's exception to obtaining a Georgia license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=6]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A02
A member of a United States military reserve component may operate a government-owned or leased motor vehicle under the licensing exception when performing reserve duties. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=6]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A02
During the driving examination to obtain a license, the applicant must be accompanied by a licensed responsible adult aged at least 21, or by a certified examiner or department agent. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=6]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A02
The migrant-farm-worker exception applies to someone working in Georgia for fewer than 90 days in a calendar year who holds a valid license from another state. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=6]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A02
A Georgia resident aged at least 15 may receive actual in-car instruction in a noncommercial training vehicle under the direct personal supervision of a DDS-licensed instructor. The instructor must check an unlicensed trainee's vision before driving instruction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=6]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A02
The personal-transportation-vehicle licensing exception covers a roadway maintained only for those vehicles, or a crossing of another road at a location designated for motorized-cart crossings. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=6]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A02
The nonresident-student exception requires an age of at least 16, immediate possession of a valid home license, and an international driving permit when that license is not in English. Georgia's applicable license restrictions still govern. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=6]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A02
A student using the nonresident licensing exception must be enrolled now or in the immediately preceding enrollment period, have paid nonresident tuition for that period, and possess proof of payment. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=6]

Misconceptions: A transferred teen credential, a provisional credential and an adult credential do not share every age condition.
Mnemonic: Stop safely, keep hands visible, wait for directions.
Glossary: A restriction is a condition placed on a credential; an instructional permit identifies supervised learning privileges.
Dynamic-fact isolation: Fees, eligibility policies, travel deadlines and document rules retain dated-source review; conflicting replacement fees and garbled restriction codes are withheld.
